config.title: align-self and justify-self

intro.title: align-self and justify-self
intro.body: In this lesson, you will build a simple grid layout of colored boxes to practice controlling the placement of individual items within a CSS Grid container. You will learn the core concepts of align-self and justify-self, which allow you to override the default alignment of a single grid item along the block (vertical) and inline (horizontal) axes, respectively. The main technology involved is CSS, specifically using properties like display: grid, align-self, and justify-self. By the end, you'll be able to precisely position items inside a grid independently from the overall container alignment.
intro.usecase: In real-world interfaces, align-self and justify-self are essential for precise control over individual items within grid layouts. Developers use these properties when building dashboards with widgets that need independent positioning, such as a metrics panel where one chart should align differently than others. They're also crucial in forms where specific form fields or buttons require custom alignment within their grid cells, like a submit button that needs to be right-justified while other elements remain centered. These properties give developers fine-grained control to handle edge cases in complex UI components like card layouts, navigation menus, and responsive panels.

objectives: Apply the align-self property to vertically position individual grid items within their cells.
Configure the justify-self property to horizontally align individual grid items within their cells.
Manipulate grid item alignment by overriding the parent container's align-items and justify-items settings.
Construct a grid layout where specific items use different self-alignment values than the default.
Initialize a CSS Grid container and selectively apply self-alignment to its child elements.
Update existing grid layouts by adjusting the align-self and justify-self properties on targeted items.
Integrate align-self and justify-self with other grid properties to achieve precise item placement.

steps.title: Create a CSS file and set up the HTML container structure
steps.instruction: Create a new CSS file and define a container with grid display properties
steps.hint: Start by creating a CSS file and setting up a container class with display: grid to establish a grid layout.
steps.seedCode: /* Create a CSS file and define a container with grid display properties */
steps.expectedOutcome: A CSS file is created with a container class that has grid display properties.
successCriteria: A .container class is defined with display: grid property.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You've started the CSS file, but make sure to define a .container class with display: grid to establish the grid layout.
steps.feedbackWrong: The CSS file doesn't contain a .container class with display: grid. Please create a container with grid display properties.

steps.title: Define the grid container with explicit rows and columns
steps.instruction: Add grid-template-rows and grid-template-columns properties to your container to create a 3x3 grid structure.
steps.hint: Use grid-template-rows: repeat(3, 1fr); and grid-template-columns: repeat(3, 1fr); to create three equal rows and three equal columns.
steps.expectedOutcome: The container will have a defined 3x3 grid structure with equal-sized rows and columns.
successCriteria: The container has both grid-template-rows: repeat(3, 1fr); and grid-template-columns: repeat(3, 1fr); properties.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track, but make sure you've added both grid-template-rows and grid-template-columns properties with repeat(3, 1fr) values.
steps.feedbackWrong: The grid structure isn't properly defined. Check that you've added both grid-template-rows and grid-template-columns properties.

steps.title: Style the grid items with basic visual properties
steps.instruction: Add CSS rules for .item to give each grid item a background color, padding, and border.
steps.hint: Create a .item selector and define properties like background-color, padding, and border.
steps.expectedOutcome: Grid items will have visual styling to make them distinct for alignment practice.
successCriteria: The .item selector exists with background-color, padding, and border properties defined.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track, but make sure to include all three: background-color, padding, and border for the .item selector.
steps.feedbackWrong: The .item selector with the required styling properties (background-color, padding, border) is missing or incomplete.

steps.title: Introduce align-self property on a specific grid item
steps.instruction: Add a CSS rule for the grid item with class 'item-a' and apply the property 'align-self: center' to vertically center it within its grid cell.
steps.hint: Create a new selector targeting '.item-a' and set the align-self property to center.
steps.expectedOutcome: The grid item with class 'item-a' will be vertically centered within its grid cell while other items remain at their default alignment.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track, but make sure you're targeting '.item-a' specifically and using the exact property 'align-self: center'.
steps.feedbackWrong: The align-self property wasn't applied correctly. Remember to create a selector for '.item-a' and set align-self to center.

steps.title: Experiment with different align-self values
steps.instruction: In the CSS file, change the align-self property for item-a to 'start' to align it to the top of its grid cell.
steps.hint: Look for the comment about align-self for item-a and replace it with a CSS rule targeting .item-a with align-self: start;
steps.expectedOutcome: The item-a grid cell will be aligned to the top (start) of its grid area vertically.
successCriteria: The CSS file contains a rule for .item-a with align-self: start;
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track, but make sure you've written a complete CSS rule for .item-a with align-self: start;
steps.feedbackWrong: The align-self property for item-a is not set to start. Check that you've written a CSS rule targeting .item-a with align-self: start;

steps.title: Introduce justify-self property on a specific grid item
steps.instruction: Add a CSS rule for .item-b to apply justify-self: center; to horizontally center it within its grid cell.
steps.hint: Create a new selector targeting .item-b and set the justify-self property to center.
steps.expectedOutcome: The item-b grid item will be horizontally centered within its cell while other items remain at their default positions.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're close! Make sure you've created a selector for .item-b and set justify-self to center.
steps.feedbackWrong: The CSS rule for item-b with justify-self: center is missing or incorrect. Try adding: .item-b { justify-self: center; }

steps.title: Experiment with different justify-self values
steps.instruction: Change the justify-self property on item-b from 'center' to 'end' to see how it affects horizontal alignment.
steps.hint: Look for the existing justify-self rule for .item-b and modify its value to 'end'.
steps.expectedOutcome: The item-b grid cell will be horizontally aligned to the end (right side) of its grid area.
successCriteria: The .item-b selector has a justify-self property with the value 'end'.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're close. Make sure you're modifying the existing .item-b rule and setting justify-self to 'end'.
steps.feedbackWrong: Check that you're editing the correct selector and property. The goal is to change justify-self from 'center' to 'end' for item-b.

steps.title: Combine align-self and justify-self on the same item
steps.instruction: Apply both align-self: center and justify-self: center to the .item-a selector to completely center it within its grid cell.
steps.hint: Add both properties to the same CSS rule. You can place them after any existing properties for .item-a.
steps.expectedOutcome: The .item-a rule will have both align-self: center and justify-self: center, allowing the item to be perfectly centered both vertically and horizontally in its grid cell.
successCriteria: The CSS rule for .item-a includes both align-self: center and justify-self: center properties.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're close! Make sure you've added both align-self: center and justify-self: center to the .item-a selector.
steps.feedbackWrong: The step requires applying both align-self: center and justify-self: center to the .item-a selector. Check that you've added both properties correctly.

steps.title: Create alignment variations across multiple grid items
steps.instruction: Apply align-self: start to item-c and justify-self: end to item-d to create distinct alignment variations across your grid items.
steps.hint: Add two new CSS rules: one for .item-c with align-self: start, and another for .item-d with justify-self: end.
steps.expectedOutcome: Item-c will align to the start of its grid cell vertically, and item-d will justify to the end of its grid cell horizontally, creating visible alignment variations.
successCriteria: Two new CSS rules are added: .item-c with align-self: start, and .item-d with justify-self: end.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track, but make sure you've added both CSS rules: one for .item-c with align-self: start, and another for .item-d with justify-self: end.
steps.feedbackWrong: The code doesn't match the expected outcome. Please add CSS rules for .item-c with align-self: start and .item-d with justify-self: end.

steps.title: Review and observe the final aligned grid layout
steps.instruction: Add align-self: center and justify-self: center to item-a to complete the demonstration of individual grid item alignment.
steps.hint: Apply both align-self and justify-self properties to the .item-a selector in your CSS.
steps.expectedOutcome: The grid layout will now show all four items with different align-self and justify-self combinations, demonstrating how individual items can be positioned independently within their grid cells.
successCriteria: item-a has both align-self: center and justify-self: center applied, completing the set of alignment examples.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're close! Make sure you've added both align-self: center and justify-self: center to the .item-a selector. Check that both properties are spelled correctly and have the value 'center'.
steps.feedbackWrong: The CSS for item-a doesn't seem to have both align-self and justify-self properties with the value 'center'. Remember to add both properties to the .item-a selector to complete the demonstration.
